title: Ad Hoc Parsing of Complex Security Formats
pattern: Hand-crafting ad hoc string splits, substring slices, or custom regexes to parse complex security-sensitive formats (like JSON, URLs, or X.509 certificates).
why_bad: Complex standards contain massive state spaces and edge cases. Ad hoc tokenizers frequently fail to parse unusual variants, leading to validation bypasses, denial-of-service panics, or memory disclosure vulnerabilities.
detection: The use of standard string tokenizing methods (`split`, `substring`, index finders) to parse complex structures on security boundaries.
fix: Rely exclusively on standard, heavily scrutinized, and fuzzed library parsers to process complex protocol configurations.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 11, p. 238-239.
